newsitem.title: COTE D'IVOIRE: Ivorian president pardons jailed journalists.
newsitem.headline: Ivorian president pardons jailed journalists.

text.p: Ivory Coast's President, Henri Konan Bedie, has pardoned three journalists accused of insulting him by suggesting his presence brought bad luck to Ivorian soccer team ASEC in the 1995 African Champions Cup final.
State radio reported on Wednesday that the pardon, a gesture for the New Year, was intended to underline Bedie's commitment to "social peace".

Abou Drahamane Sangare, Emmanuel Kore and Freedom Neruda of the opposition daily La Voie were jailed a year ago over an article on the defeat of home favourites ASEC by South Africa's Orlando Pirates in the December 1995 final in Abidjan.
Ivory Coast's second multi-party elections in 1995 were coloured by political and ethnic unrest in which 35 people died nationwide.
The West African nation, the world's top cocoa producer, finally wrapped up those elections last weekend with peaceful by-elections in areas where polling had been postponed because of the violence.
